Patients were also subgrouped based on fundus appearance within the first week of life as follows: Group A: eyes without any retinal hemorrhages (RHs) (n=13 eyes); Group B: eyes with widespread peripheral RHs sparing the macula (n=28 eyes); Group C: eyes with widespread peripheral RHs with macular involvement (n=5 eyes); Group D: healthy controls (n=40 eyes). All children underwent optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA)(Solix Visionix). FAZ area, foveal vessel densities and central foveal thickness (CFT) were compared.

Results

Foveal vessel density of the superficial capillary plexus (VD-SCP) and CFT were significantly higher in Group 2 compared with Group 1 (all p<0.05). Significantly smaller FAZ area was noted in Group 2 (0.19±0.09 mm2) compared with Group 1 (0.28±0.10 mm2) and 3 (0.26±0.09 mm2)(all p<0.05).

Conclusions

HIE may lead to persistent alterations in foveal microvasculature. OCTA may serve as a non-invasive biomarker for detecting long-term retinal microvascular sequelae in children with a history of perinatal asphyxia.

records.title: EFFICACY AND SAFETY OF SUBTHRESHOLD LASER IN PATIENTS WITH ACUTE CENTRAL SEROUS CHORIORETINOPATHY: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

content.title: EFFICACY AND SAFETY OF SUBTHRESHOLD LASER IN PATIENTS WITH ACUTE CENTRAL SEROUS CHORIORETINOPATHY: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Subthreshold laser has been proposed as a potentially safer and more effective alternative for patients with acute central serous chorioretinopathy (CSC). Hence, the objective of this systematic review was to assess the efficacy and safety of subthreshold laser treatment for acute CSC.

Methods

We performed a comprehensive systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, and CENTRAL from their inception up to March 24, 2026. We included randomized controlled trials comparing the efficacy and/or safety of subthreshold laser against any comparator. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted, and the certainty of evidence was rated using the minimally contextualized GRADE approach.

Results

Six randomized controlled trials (401 participants) in patients with acute CSC were included. Compared with conventional laser, subthreshold laser probably yields similar improvements in visual acuity and reduces retinal pigment epithelium damage but probably leads to a lower rate of subretinal fluid resolution. When compared with observation, subthreshold laser may result in similar visual acuity outcomes but may reduce persistent metamorphopsia and increase subretinal fluid resolution, although the certainty of evidence is very low. Compared with half-dose photodynamic therapy, subthreshold laser may provide comparable visual outcomes but lower anatomical improvement, with very low certainty of evidence.

Conclusion

In acute CSC, subthreshold laser appears safer than conventional laser and produces similar visual outcomes, although its anatomical efficacy is limited. Its potential advantages over observation or photodynamic therapy remain uncertain because of low-certainty evidence.

records.title: Interpretable Machine Learning for Course Prediction in Central Serous Chorioretinopathy Using Baseline Optical Coherence Tomography From a Multicenter Cohort.

content.title: Interpretable Machine Learning for Course Prediction in Central Serous Chorioretinopathy Using Baseline Optical Coherence Tomography From a Multicenter Cohort.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To predict disease clinical course in central serous chorioretinopathy (CSC) using an interpretable machine learning model applied to baseline artificial intelligence (AI)-derived optical coherence tomography (OCT) biomarkers acquired at first presentation.

Design

Multicenter, retrospective cohort study.

Participants

Overall, 329 treatment-naïve CSC eyes recruited across 8 international centers in Europe, the Middle East, Asia, and North Africa.

Methods

Treatment-naïve CSC patients were retrospectively included and classified, based on follow-up, as acute or chronic CSC according to subretinal fluid (SRF) resolution. Baseline OCT biomarkers were extracted using an AI-based platform (Discovery OCT Biomarker Detector; RetinAI AG, Switzerland), which quantified retinal layer thicknesses, including the outer nuclear layer (ONL) and photoreceptor-retinal pigment epithelium (PR + RPE) complex, fluid volumes (SRF and RPE detachment [PED]), and biomarker probabilities, across central, parafoveal, and perifoveal ETDRS regions. These features used to develop an interpretable machine learning model predicting future CSC chronicity.

Main outcome measures

Classification of eyes as acute or chronic CSC, determined by SRF resolution on follow-up; discriminative performance of the Random Forest classifier, assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC); and biomarker importance, evaluated using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values.

Results

Of 329 eyes (291 patients), 92 (28.0%) were classified as acute and 237 (72.0%) as chronic CSC; mean follow-up was 4.2 ± 1.6 years. Chronic CSC patients were significantly older (51.7 ± 12.6 vs 43.2 ± 9.6 years, P < .001) with worse baseline visual acuity (0.25 ± 0.21 vs 0.16 ± 0.15 logMAR, P = .029). Among baseline OCT biomarkers, parafoveal ONL thickness showed the strongest association with disease chronicity (q < 0.0001; r = -0.414). The Random Forest classifier achieved an AUC of 0.852 (95% CI: 0.748-0.940). SHAP analysis identified parafoveal ONL thickness, perifoveal PR + RPE thickness, and central SRF volume as the strongest predictors of acute CSC, whereas greater RNFL thickness, PED volume, FLAT PED probability, and HF probability were the most influential predictors of chronic disease.

Conclusions

Automatically detected OCT biomarkers can predict CSC chronicity at initial presentation with good discriminatory performance. Quantitative markers of outer retinal integrity, fluid configuration, and RPE dysfunction may improve prognostication, facilitate patient counseling, and help identify individuals at increased risk of persistent CSC.

records.title: 3D Corneal and Retinal Bioprinting: Tissue Engineering Strategies, Translational Challenges, and Clinical Opportunities.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: 3D Corneal and Retinal Bioprinting: Tissue Engineering Strategies, Translational Challenges, and Clinical Opportunities.
content.abstract: Three-dimensional bioprinting has emerged as a promising strategy for addressing major unmet needs in ophthalmology, including the global shortage of donor corneal tissue and the absence of restorative therapies for retinal degenerative disease. Advances in biomaterials, stem cell biology, and biofabrication have enabled increasingly sophisticated ocular constructs, ranging from engineered corneal grafts to multicellular retinal models that recapitulate key aspects of native tissue architecture. However, substantial challenges remain in reproducing the optical, mechanical, and biological functions required for clinical translation. This review critically evaluates the current state of corneal and retinal bioprinting through a framework organized around tissue target, fabrication modality, and intended application. Major bioprinting approaches, including extrusion-based, laser-assisted, drop-on-demand, and light-based technologies, are compared with respect to resolution, cell compatibility, scalability, and translational potential. Particular emphasis is placed on the engineering constraints governing construct fidelity, bioink design, tissue integration, and long-term functional performance. Current evidence suggests that corneal and retinal bioprinting have progressed along distinct translational trajectories. Corneal bioprinting has achieved encouraging preclinical outcomes, with selected approaches entering early clinical evaluation, whereas retinal bioprinting has generated highly informative disease models but remains at an earlier stage of translational development. Across both tissues, the field has increasingly shifted from reproducing individual cellular components toward reconstructing the biological interfaces and multicellular systems that underlie tissue function. Future progress will depend on establishing functional validation frameworks, reproducible manufacturing workflows, and standardized benchmarks to support the clinical development of vision-restoring bioprinted constructs.

records.title: Seeing in tandem: Cis and trans-regulation of tandemly-duplicated cone opsin genes in zebrafish.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Seeing in tandem: Cis and trans-regulation of tandemly-duplicated cone opsin genes in zebrafish.
content.abstract: The molecular basis for vertebrate color vision is expression of spectrally-selective opsin-based photopigments within distinct cone photoreceptor populations. In several primates including humans, and in numerous fish species, genes encoding duplicated, spectrally-divergent cone opsin proteins may be positioned in tandem arrays. This article reviews studies of the regulation of differential expression of these duplicated cone opsin genes in humans and fish, with an emphasis on knowledge derived from the zebrafish model. In humans, the long wavelength-sensitive/medium wavelength-sensitive (LWS/MWS; red/green) tandemly-duplicated array underlies trichromatic color vision; mutations in this array cause altered color vision and retinal degenerations. A foundational model posited that regulation of human LWS vs. MWS opsin expression is stochastic, whereby an upstream enhancer associates randomly with promoters of the proximal or distal gene, and one of these associations becomes permanent. Discoveries of tandemly-duplicated cone opsin genes in teleost fish, including the versatile zebrafish model, led to their use to further pursue mechanisms of differential expression. The tandemly-duplicated zebrafish lws1 and lws2 genes (encoding red-sensing cone opsins) share a common ancestral gene with human LWS and MWS. Subsequent studies revealed that differential expression of these genes is regulated by the paracrine signal retinoic acid (RA) and the endocrine signal thyroid hormone (TH). Further investigations identified additional cone transcripts distinguishing zebrafish LWS1 vs. LWS2 cones, plasticity of cone opsin expression across the lifespan in response to TH, and a candidate receptor and cis-regulatory element. The findings warrant updates to the foundational model and further consideration of hypotheses for regulation of the human LWS vs. MWS genes.

records.title: Ocular Changes in Human Spaceflight.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Ocular Changes in Human Spaceflight.
content.abstract: Spaceflight presents unique challenges to ocular health, with astronauts experiencing a range of visual disturbances in the setting of microgravity, radiation exposure, and other environmental factors. This review synthesizes knowledge about how spaceflight affects ocular anatomy and function. We outline the diagnostic and therapeutic limitations in microgravity, including constraints on imaging modalities, intracranial pressure measurement, and drug delivery. In addition, we examine common spaceflight-associated ocular pathologies, including spaceflight-associated neuro-ocular syndrome, corneal epithelial disruption, possible radiation-associated lens changes, and retinal or choroidal alterations. Drawing from evidence across human missions, terrestrial analogs, and experimental models, this review emphasizes the critical importance of vision to astronaut safety and mission success. Future directions include long-term ocular health monitoring, advancement of in-flight diagnostic capabilities, and multidisciplinary strategies to safeguard astronaut vision.

records.title: AI-ASSISTED OCT BIOMARKER QUANTIFICATION REVEALS DISTINCT RETINAL FLUID TRAJECTORIES IN CENTRAL RETINAL VEIN OCCLUSION.

content.title: AI-ASSISTED OCT BIOMARKER QUANTIFICATION REVEALS DISTINCT RETINAL FLUID TRAJECTORIES IN CENTRAL RETINAL VEIN OCCLUSION.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To characterize longitudinal patterns of intraretinal (IRF) and subretinal fluid (SRF) dynamics using artificial intelligence-assisted optical coherence tomography (OCT) biomarker quantification and to evaluate their association with long-term visual outcomes in eyes with central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO).

Methods

Patients with previously treatment-naïve CRVO and a documented 24-month follow-up were retrospectively included. All eyes received intravitreal aflibercept administered according to a treat-and-extend protocol. Spectral-domain OCT scans were analyzed at baseline and after 3 and 24 months. IRF and SRF volumes were quantified using RetinAI Discovery OCT Biomarker Detector (Ikerian AG). Linear regression models were used to assess the association between fluid volumes and 24-month corrected distance visual acuity (CDVA). Patients were clustered according to their IRF trajectories over time to identify distinct fluid-response phenotypes.

Results

Out of 173 patients, 64 eyes (64 patients) were included. Baseline IRF and SRF volumes showed no significant association with 24-month CDVA. Cluster analysis of longitudinal IRF trajectories identified four distinct fluid-response patterns. Eyes with low or rapidly resolving IRF achieved the best long-term visual outcomes (median CDVA 73 letters), whereas those with persistent or recurrent IRF showed poorer outcomes (median 53 letters; P = 0.008). Early IRF resolution tended to predict superior visual recovery at 24 months.

Conclusion

Artificial intelligence-based volumetric OCT analysis suggests that distinct retinal fluid trajectories in CRVO may have prognostic implications for long-term visual acuity, although these findings are preliminary and require validation. Dynamic IRF resolution patterns may be more informative than static fluid volumes for predicting functional outcomes after anti-vascular endothelial growth factor therapy.

records.title: Association of Retinal Microvascular Density with Hemodynamic and Clinical Severity Markers in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.

content.title: Association of Retinal Microvascular Density with Hemodynamic and Clinical Severity Markers in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate whether quantitative retinal microvascular and structural parameters, measured by optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA), are associated with disease severity and right ventriculo-arterial coupling in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH).

Methods

This cross-sectional study included 45 patients with confirmed PAH, stratified by New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class (I-III). Patients with coexisting ocular pathologies were strictly excluded. Vessel density (VD) in the superficial (SCP) and deep capillary plexuses (DCP), foveal avascular zone characteristics, and ganglion cell complex (GCC) thickness were analyzed. These parameters were correlated with functional capacity (6-minute walk test [6-mWT]), NT-proBNP levels, and the echocardiographic TAPSE/sPAP ratio.

Results

Retinal VD in both SCP and DCP progressively decreased with worsening NYHA functional class (p < 0.05). Retinal VD showed a significant negative correlation with NT-proBNP levels (r = -0.355, p = 0.017) and a positive correlation with 6-mWT distance (r = 0.499, p < 0.001). Crucially, retinal microvascular density demonstrated a robust positive correlation with the TAPSE/sPAP ratio (r = 0.420, p = 0.004), a surrogate for right ventriculo-arterial coupling. GCC thickness exhibited variations across NYHA classes but lacked a consistent linear progression.

Conclusion

Retinal microvascular attenuation in PAH is strongly associated not only with functional and biochemical severity but also with central hemodynamic impairment represented by the TAPSE/sPAP ratio. These findings suggest that OCTA-derived vessel density may serve as a promising, non-invasive biomarker for monitoring systemic microvascular compromise and right heart function in PAH.

records.title: Choroidal Thickness and Axial Length as Independent Correlates of AMD: Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2017-2020.

content.title: Choroidal Thickness and Axial Length as Independent Correlates of AMD: Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2017-2020.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To examine how choroidal thickness and axial length relate to age-related macular degeneration (AMD) across disease stages in a nationwide Korean population.

Design

Cross-sectional, population-based study.

Methods

We analyzed the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey, 2017-2020, including 15,388 adults aged 40 years or older with gradable fundus photographs; ocular analyses included 13,807 after excluding coexisting macular disease. Axial length (AL), central macular thickness (CMT), and subfoveal choroidal thickness (SFCT) were measured by partial coherence interferometry and optical coherence tomography. Associations were assessed by survey-weighted logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, and systemic factors.

Results

Weighted AMD prevalence was 14.41% (95% CI, 13.67-15.15; early, 13.46%; late, 0.95%). In multivariable models, greater SFCT was associated with early AMD (OR per 10 µm, 1.03; 95% CI, 1.02-1.03; P < .001), and shorter AL with early AMD (OR per 1 mm, 0.76; 0.71-0.82; P < .001) and late AMD (0.74; 0.57-0.97; P = .030). Greater CMT was associated with late AMD (OR per 10 µm, 1.10; 1.01-1.19; P = .030) and neovascular AMD (1.23; 1.12-1.35; P < .001). SFCT and AL remained associated with early AMD after mutual adjustment (both P < .001). Older age, male sex, non-white-collar occupation, and rural residence were associated with AMD, and anemia with late AMD (1.78; 1.06-2.96; P = .028).

Conclusions

Greater SFCT and shorter AL were independently associated with early AMD. These findings suggest that choroidal thickness and axial length may reflect distinct structural correlates.

records.title: METASTATIC UROTHELIAL CARCINOMA OF THE BLADDER TO THE RETINA: A CLINICOPATHOLOGIC CORRELATION AND REVIEW OF THE LITERATURE.

content.title: METASTATIC UROTHELIAL CARCINOMA OF THE BLADDER TO THE RETINA: A CLINICOPATHOLOGIC CORRELATION AND REVIEW OF THE LITERATURE.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To report a rare case of metastatic urothelial carcinoma of the bladder (UCB) to the retina confirmed with histopathology and compare diagnostic findings, therapeutic techniques, and prognosis to other reported retinal and ocular metastatic cases, with focus on urothelial origin.

Methods

Intravenous fluorescein angiography (IVFA) was used to investigate a large yellow-white superotemporal retinal lesion OS. Two pars plana vitrectomies OS were performed yielding vitreous cytology and retinal lesion biopsy histopathology, respectively.

Results

IVFA showed overlying vitreous debris blockage, punctate hyperfluorescence consistent with light-bulb microaneurysms, patchy capillary nonperfusion, hemorrhagic blockage, and late central leakage. Vitreous cytology revealed atypical cells characterized by enlarged, pleomorphic nuclei, abundant cytoplasm, and harboring common cell borders. Retina biopsy revealed invasive irregular islands of carcinomatous cells with immunoreactivity to high molecular weight cytokeratin, uroplakin III, and GATA-3; the same cells were CK20 negative.

Conclusion

We report the second documented case, to our knowledge, of retinal metastasis from UCB. The clinical pattern and presentation fit similarly to the first documented case.

records.title: Advances in understanding the molecular structure of retinoschisin while questions remain of biological function.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Advances in understanding the molecular structure of retinoschisin while questions remain of biological function.
content.abstract: Retinoschisin (RS1) is a secreted protein that is essential for maintaining integrity of the retina. Numerous mutations in RS1 cause X-linked retinoschisis (XLRS), a progressive degeneration of the retina that leads to vision loss in young males. A key manifestation of XLRS is the formation of cavities (cysts) in the retina and separation of the layers (schisis), disrupting synaptic transmission. There are currently no approved treatments for patients with XLRS. Strategies using adeno-associated viral (AAV) vectors to deliver functional copies of RS1 as a form of gene augmentation therapy, are under clinical evaluation. To improve therapeutic strategies for treating XLRS, it is critical to better understand the secretion of RS1 and its molecular function. Immunofluorescence and immunoelectron microscopy show that RS1 is located on the surfaces of the photoreceptor inner segments and bipolar cells. Sequence homology indicates a discoidin domain fold, similar to many other proteins with demonstrated adhesion functions. Recent structural studies revealed the tertiary structure of RS1 as two back-to-back octameric rings, each cross-linked by disulfides. The observation of higher order structures in vitro suggests the formation of an adhesive matrix spanning the distance between cells (∼100 nm). Several studies indicated that RS1 readily binds to other proteins such as the sodium-potassium ATPase (NaK-ATPase) and extracellular matrix proteins. Alternatively, RS1 may influence fluid regulation via interaction with membrane proteins such as the NaK-ATPase, largely inferred from the use of carbonic anhydrase inhibitors to shrink the typical intra-retinal cysts in XLRS. We discuss these models in light of RS1 structure and address the difficulty in understanding the function of RS1.

records.title: Female carriers of X-linked inherited retinal diseases - Genetics, diagnosis, and potential therapies.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Female carriers of X-linked inherited retinal diseases - Genetics, diagnosis, and potential therapies.
content.abstract: Inherited retinal diseases (IRDs) are a group of heterogeneous conditions that cause progressive vision loss, typically due to monogenic mutations. Female carriers of X-linked IRDs have a single copy of the disease-causing gene, and therefore, may exhibit variable clinical signs that vary from near normal retina to severe disease and vision loss. The relationships between individual genetic mutations and disease severity in X-linked carriers requires further study. This review summarises the current literature surrounding the spectrum of disease seen in female carriers of choroideremia and X-linked retinitis pigmentosa. Various classification systems are contrasted to accurately grade retinal disease. Furthermore, genetic mechanisms at the early embryonic stage are explored to potentially explain the variability of disease seen in female carriers. Future research in this area will provide insight into the association between genotype and retinal phenotypes of female carriers, which will guide in the management of these patients. This review acknowledges the importance of identifying which patients may be at high risk of developing severe symptoms, and therefore should be considered for emerging treatments, such as retinal gene therapy.

records.title: Association Between Diabetic Retinopathy, Brain Structural Abnormalities, and Cognitive Impairment for Accumulated Evidence in Observational Studies.

content.title: Association Between Diabetic Retinopathy, Brain Structural Abnormalities, and Cognitive Impairment for Accumulated Evidence in Observational Studies.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the association between diabetic retinopathy (DR) and cerebral disease or cognitive impairment.

Design

Systematic review and meta-analysis.

Method

The hypothesis was formulated prior to data collection. Cross-sectional studies and cohort studies that assessed the association between any measure of DR and cerebral small vessel disease or any type of cognitive impairment in diabetic participants were included. The data were independently extracted by two investigators. This systematic review and meta-analysis adhered to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses and Meta-analysis of Observational Studies in Epidemiology guidelines RESULTS: A total of 27 studies were included. The combined odds ratio of 5 cross-sectional/cohort studies that reported that the associations between DR and cerebral structural changes was 1.75 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.36-2.25). The combined hazard ratio of 4 cohort studies that examined the association between DR and cognitive impairment events was 1.47 (95% CI: 1.22-1.78). The combined odds ratio of 14 cross-sectional/cohort studies that examined the association between DR and different cognitive impairment events was 1.43 (95% CI: 1.06-1.93). The overall coefficient (β) of 4 studies that examined the relationship between DR and specific cognitive performance was 0.09 (95% CI: 0.00-0.18). Considering the quality of the data, we have performed subgroup analysis in studies scored >7 and studies scored ≤7, respectively, according to the Newcastle-Ottawa scale.

Conclusion

The present meta-analysis suggests that DR is associated with an increased risk of structural abnormalities in the brain and cognitive impairment. This association remained significant after adjusting for blood glucose, and the presence of hypertension, indicating that DR is an important danger signal for cerebral abnormalities.

records.title: Trustworthy AI: Closing the gap between development and integration of AI systems in ophthalmic practice.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Trustworthy AI: Closing the gap between development and integration of AI systems in ophthalmic practice.
content.abstract: An increasing number of artificial intelligence (AI) systems are being proposed in ophthalmology, motivated by the variety and amount of clinical and imaging data, as well as their potential benefits at the different stages of patient care. Despite achieving close or even superior performance to that of experts, there is a critical gap between development and integration of AI systems in ophthalmic practice. This work focuses on the importance of trustworthy AI to close that gap. We identify the main aspects or challenges that need to be considered along the AI design pipeline so as to generate systems that meet the requirements to be deemed trustworthy, including those concerning accuracy, resiliency, reliability, safety, and accountability. We elaborate on mechanisms and considerations to address those aspects or challenges, and define the roles and responsibilities of the different stakeholders involved in AI for ophthalmic care, i.e., AI developers, reading centers, healthcare providers, healthcare institutions, ophthalmological societies and working groups or committees, patients, regulatory bodies, and payers. Generating trustworthy AI is not a responsibility of a sole stakeholder. There is an impending necessity for a collaborative approach where the different stakeholders are represented along the AI design pipeline, from the definition of the intended use to post-market surveillance after regulatory approval. This work contributes to establish such multi-stakeholder interaction and the main action points to be taken so that the potential benefits of AI reach real-world ophthalmic settings.

records.title: Activation of retinal glial cells contributes to the degeneration of ganglion cells in experimental glaucoma.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Activation of retinal glial cells contributes to the degeneration of ganglion cells in experimental glaucoma.
content.abstract: Elevation of intraocular pressure (IOP) is a major risk factor for neurodegeneration in glaucoma. Glial cells, which play an important role in normal functioning of retinal neurons, are well involved into retinal ganglion cell (RGC) degeneration in experimental glaucoma animal models generated by elevated IOP. In response to elevated IOP, mGluR I is first activated and Kir4.1 channels are subsequently inhibited, which leads to the activation of Müller cells. Müller cell activation is followed by a complex process, including proliferation, release of inflammatory and growth factors (gliosis). Gliosis is further regulated by several factors. Activated Müller cells contribute to RGC degeneration through generating glutamate receptor-mediated excitotoxicity, releasing cytotoxic factors and inducing microglia activation. Elevated IOP activates microglia, and following morphological and functional changes, these cells, as resident immune cells in the retina, show adaptive immune responses, including an enhanced release of pro-inflammatory factors (tumor neurosis factor-α, interleukins, etc.). These ATP and Toll-like receptor-mediated responses are further regulated by heat shock proteins, CD200R, chemokine receptors, and metabotropic purinergic receptors, may aggravate RGC loss. In the optic nerve head, astrogliosis is initiated and regulated by a complex reaction process, including purines, transmitters, chemokines, growth factors and cytokines, which contributes to RGC axon injury through releasing pro-inflammatory factors and changing extracellular matrix in glaucoma. The effects of activated glial cells on RGCs are further modified by the interplay among different types of glial cells. This review is concluded by presenting an in-depth discussion of possible research directions in this field in the future.

records.title: Toward Universal Eye Health Coverage-Key Outcomes of the World Health Organization Package of Eye Care Interventions: A Systematic Review.

content.title: Toward Universal Eye Health Coverage-Key Outcomes of the World Health Organization Package of Eye Care Interventions: A Systematic Review.
content.abstract:
Importance

Despite persistent inequalities in access to eye care services globally, guidance on a set of recommended, evidence-based eye care interventions to support country health care planning has not been available. To overcome this barrier, the World Health Organization (WHO) Package of Eye Care Interventions (PECI) has been developed.

Objective

To describe the key outcomes of the PECI development.

Evidence review

A standardized stepwise approach that included the following stages: (1) selection of priority eye conditions by an expert panel after reviewing epidemiological evidence and health facility data; (2) identification of interventions and related evidence for the selected eye conditions from a systematic review of clinical practice guidelines (CPGs); stage 2 included a systematic literature search, screening of title and abstracts (excluding articles that were not relevant CPGs), full-text review to assess disclosure of conflicts of interest and affiliations, quality appraisal, and data extraction; (3) expert review of the evidence extracted in stage 2, identification of missed interventions, and agreement on the inclusion of essential interventions suitable for implementation in low- and middle-income resource settings; and (4) peer review.

Findings

Fifteen priority eye conditions were chosen. The literature search identified 3601 articles. Of these, 469 passed title and abstract screening, 151 passed full-text screening, 98 passed quality appraisal, and 87 were selected for data extraction. Little evidence (≤1 CPG identified) was available for pterygium, keratoconus, congenital eyelid disorders, vision rehabilitation, myopic macular degeneration, ptosis, entropion, and ectropion. In stage 3, domain-specific expert groups voted to include 135 interventions (57%) of a potential 235 interventions collated from stage 2. After synthesis across all interventions and eye conditions, 64 interventions (13 health promotion and education, 6 screening and prevention, 38 treatment, and 7 rehabilitation) were included in the PECI.

Conclusions and relevance

This systematic review of CPGs for priority eye conditions, followed by an expert consensus procedure, identified 64 essential, evidence-based, eye care interventions that are required to achieve universal eye health coverage. The review identified some important gaps, including a paucity of high-quality, English-language CPGs, for several eye diseases and a dearth of evidence-based recommendations on eye health promotion and prevention within existing CPGs.

records.title: The impact of sensory neuropathy and inflammation on epithelial wound healing in diabetic corneas.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: The impact of sensory neuropathy and inflammation on epithelial wound healing in diabetic corneas.
content.abstract: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) is the most common complication of diabetes, with several underlying pathophysiological mechanisms, some of which are still uncertain. The cornea is an avascular tissue and sensitive to hyperglycemia, resulting in several diabetic corneal complications including delayed epithelial wound healing, recurrent erosions, neuropathy, loss of sensitivity, and tear film changes. The manifestation of DPN in the cornea is referred to as diabetic neurotrophic keratopathy (DNK). Recent studies have revealed that disturbed epithelial-neural-immune cell interactions are a major cause of DNK. The epithelium is supplied by a dense network of sensory nerve endings and dendritic cell processes, and it secretes growth/neurotrophic factors and cytokines to nourish these neighboring cells. In turn, sensory nerve endings release neuropeptides to suppress inflammation and promote epithelial wound healing, while resident immune cells provide neurotrophic and growth factors to support neuronal and epithelial cells, respectively. Diabetes greatly perturbs these interdependencies, resulting in suppressed epithelial proliferation, sensory neuropathy, and a decreased density of dendritic cells. Clinically, this results in a markedly delayed wound healing and impaired sensory nerve regeneration in response to insult and injury. Current treatments for DPN and DNK largely focus on managing the severe complications of the disease. Cell-based therapies hold promise for providing more effective treatment for diabetic keratopathy and corneal ulcers.

records.title: Influence of capsular tension ring implantation on dynamic in vivo capsular apposition and intraocular lens behavior in highly myopic eyes.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Influence of capsular tension ring implantation on dynamic in vivo capsular apposition and intraocular lens behavior in highly myopic eyes.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the dynamic in vivo capsular apposition to the intraocular lens (IOL) in highly myopic eyes after capsular tension ring (CTR) implantation using swept-source optical coherence tomography (SS-OCT), and to investigate its correlation with in-the-bag IOL behavior.

Setting

Eye Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University, Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province, China.

Design

Prospective randomized clinical trial.

Methods

Highly myopic patients undergoing cataract surgery were randomized to receive CTR implantation or not. SS-OCT was performed at 1 day, 1 week, 1 month, 3 months, and 6 months to assess capsular apposition. Postoperative aqueous depth (PAD), IOL rotation, and anterior and posterior capsular opacification (ACO/PCO) were evaluated at each follow-up visit.

Results

A total of 29 eyes with CTR implantation and 30 eyes without CTR were included. The CTR group exhibited accelerated anterior capsular apposition, demonstrated by a smaller lens-anterior capsule distance (LCD) at 1 day and a higher proportion of anterior capsular apposition at 1 week. From 1 month onward, posterior capsular apposition occurred more frequently in the CTR group. At 1 day, the average LCD positively correlated with both PAD and IOL rotation. During subsequent follow-up period, the mean capsular bend index exhibited negative correlations with the absolute changes in PAD and IOL rotational speed. The CTR group developed less severe ACO, eyes with incomplete posterior capsular apposition had a higher risk of PCO.

Conclusions

CTR implantation facilitates accelerated anterior and more complete posterior capsular apposition to the IOL in highly myopic eyes, which may contribute to improved postoperative IOL stability and a reduced incidence of capsular opacification.

records.title: Comparison of the Moussa Intraocular Lens Formula to contemporary formulas in a multicenter study.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Comparison of the Moussa Intraocular Lens Formula to contemporary formulas in a multicenter study.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the refractive predictive accuracy of the Moussa intraocular lens (IOL) formula compared with Kane, EVO, PEARL-DGS, K6, Hoffer-QST, and Barrett Universal II (BUII).

Setting

Birmingham Midland Eye Centre (Birmingham), Manchester Royal Eye Hospital and Newmedica (Manchester), UK.

Design

Multicenter, retrospective, consecutive, nonrandomized observational case series (September 2022-June 2025).

Methods

Included were one eye per patient undergoing uncomplicated phacoemulsification. Preoperative biometry used the IOLMaster 700, Lenstar LS900, or Pentacam AXL Wave. Lens-constants were optimized to zero mean prediction error (PE) for each formula and lens-biometer combination. Primary outcome was mean absolute error (MAE), evaluated using heteroscedastic studentized bootstrap analysis (2000 iterations; Holm correction). Secondary outcomes included median absolute error, root-mean-square error, standard deviation of PE, and proportions of eyes within ±0.25diopter (D) and ±0.50D.

Results

Included were 2550 patients (2550 eyes; mean age 74.0±10.0 years; 1068 male patients [41.9%]). Moussa produced a lower MAE (0.348 D) than Kane (0.359D), EVO (0.363D), PEARL-DGS (0.367D), K6 (0.367D), Hoffer-QST (0.377D), and BUII (0.379D; all p<.001). In short eyes (≤22.0mm), Moussa (0.412D) demonstrated lower error than K6 (p<.001), BUII (p<.001), Hoffer-QST (p=.008), EVO (p=.008), PEARL-DGS (p=.014), and Kane (p=.039). In long eyes (≥26.0 mm), Moussa (0.342 D) had lower error than Kane, BUII, Hoffer-QST (all p<.001), and K6 (p=.045), but not EVO (p=.068) or PEARL-DGS (p=.202).

Conclusions

The Moussa formula demonstrated high predictive accuracy across multiple biometry platforms, with statistically lower overall MAE than the comparator formulas. Absolute differences from the closest-performing formulas were modest, and ±0.50D outcomes were similar to Kane and EVO. These findings support Moussa as a clinically relevant contemporary option for IOL power calculation, with encouraging results in short and long eyes requiring further targeted validation.

records.title: Preloaded vs manually loaded intraocular lens delivery failure modes: analysis of U.S. Food and Drug Administration device reports.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Preloaded vs manually loaded intraocular lens delivery failure modes: analysis of U.S. Food and Drug Administration device reports.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare reported intraoperative failure-mode profiles between preloaded and manually loaded intraocular lens (IOL) delivery systems using U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) device reports.

Setting

FDA Manufacturer and User Facility Device Experience (MAUDE) database, United States.

Design

Retrospective cross-sectional study.

Methods

MAUDE reports from January 1, 2016, through December 31, 2025, were reviewed. Reports describing intraoperative IOL loading, delivery, or positioning issues were included when injector type was specified. Structured MAUDE fields served as the primary data source, and free-text narratives were analyzed using automated natural language processing to supplement classification when consistent with structured fields. Comparisons were performed using within-group proportions, and multivariate logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs) controlling for report year, manufacturer, lens platform, and reporting entity.

Results

Of 57 435 FDA device reports, 14 460 intraoperative reports met inclusion criteria: 10 567 (73.1%) involved preloaded systems and 3893 (26.9%) manually loaded systems. Manually loaded systems showed higher reporting of IOL damage (66.0% vs 45.4%; aOR 3.06, 95% CI 2.78-3.37; P < .001) and loading issues (aOR 5.53, 95% CI 3.99-7.66; P < .001). Preloaded systems showed higher reporting of delivery failures (40.5% vs 21.8%; aOR 3.91, 95% CI 3.51-4.35; P < .001), lens positioning issues (aOR 1.27, 95% CI 1.01-1.62; P = .041), and material or optics abnormalities (aOR 3.53, 95% CI 1.96-6.35; P < .001).

Conclusions

Preloaded and manually loaded IOL delivery systems demonstrated distinct failure-mode profiles within FDA device reports. These findings characterized reporting patterns rather than population-level risk and may inform device design and postmarket surveillance priorities.

records.title: Improving effective lens position prediction for secondary intraocular lens implantation in pediatric aphakic eyes.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Improving effective lens position prediction for secondary intraocular lens implantation in pediatric aphakic eyes.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To improve the accuracy of refractive prediction for pediatric secondary sulcus intraocular lens (IOL) implantation by optimizing the effective lens position (ELP) prediction within the SRK/T formula.

Setting

Zhongshan Ophthalmic Center, Guangzhou, China.

Design

Retrospective consecutive case-series.

Methods

The value of sulcus-ELP was identified by linear regression formula with utilizing back-calculated ELP. The obtained sulcus-ELP was subsequently incorporated into the original SRK/T formula, then creating the sulcus-SRK/T formula. The prediction accuracy of sulcus-SRK/T formula was compared with six formulas. Main outcome measures included prediction error (PE), mean error (ME), median absolute error (MedAE), and the percentage of eyes with prediction error within ±0.50 diopters (D) and ±1.00 D.

Results

This study included 86 pediatric patients (131 eyes) who underwent secondary ciliary sulcus IOL implantation. With the modified formula, the percentages of eyes achieving the prediction error (PE) within ±0.50 D and ±1.00 D were 25.6% and 53.9%, respectively, significantly higher than those of other formulas. The mean error (ME) of the modified formula was 0.46±1.39 D, and the modified formula showed lower median absolute error (MedAE) (0.95 D, P < .05) than other formulas.

Conclusions

By optimizing ELP prediction of the SRK/T formula, the prediction accuracy of pediatric secondary sulcus IOL implantation has been improved. The sulcus-SRK/T formula is a worthwhile choice and requires further external validation to confirm its effectiveness.

records.title: Clinical Features, Phenotypic Spectrum, and Associated Factors in Histopathologically Confirmed Dead Bag Syndrome.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Clinical Features, Phenotypic Spectrum, and Associated Factors in Histopathologically Confirmed Dead Bag Syndrome.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To characterize the demographic, ocular, systemic, and histopathologic features of patients undergoing surgery for late intraocular lens (IOL) instability with clinically suspected dead bag syndrome (DBS).

Setting

Private ophthalmology practice and tertiary ophthalmic pathology laboratory.

Design

Single-center consecutive case series with prospective tissue collection and retrospective chart review.

Methods

Capsular bag remnants were explanted during secondary IOL surgery and submitted for histopathologic examination. Demographic, ocular, and systemic characteristics were obtained from the medical record. Lens epithelial cell (LEC) status was graded as 0 = absent; 1 = rare residual LECs; 2 = focal identifiable LEC segments. Specimens were assessed for capsular splitting/schisis, cortical material, and anterior capsular fibrous metaplasia. Exploratory clinical comparisons were performed between LEC grade 0 and LEC grade 1-2 subgroups.

Results

Thirty-one eyes from 26 patients underwent secondary IOL surgery for late IOL subluxation or dislocation with clinical suspicion of DBS, including 27 with histopathologic evaluation. Mean age at secondary surgery was 70.5 ± 10.5 years and 80.7% patients were male. Median time from cataract surgery to presentation was 13.0 years (IQR 9.0-16.5). Axial myopia was present in 6/31 eyes (19.4%). Atopy was documented in 9/31 (29.0%), prior radiation or chemotherapy exposure in 8/31 (25.8%), autoimmune disease in 10/31 (32.3%), and ACE inhibitor or ARB use in 14/31 (45.2%). Complete LEC absence (grade 0) was present in 8/27 (29.6%), while 19/27 (70.4%) demonstrated residual LECs and/or cortical material (grades 1-2). Spontaneous posterior capsular rupture was documented in 15/31 (48.4%) cases and in 15/27 (55.6%) histopathology-confirmed cases. Atopy was more frequent in LEC grade 0 than among LEC grade 1-2 eyes (37.5% vs 15.8%; P = 0.32), though this did not reach statistical significance.

Conclusions

DBS represents a histopathologically definable spectrum of capsular degeneration characterized by LEC depletion and capsular splitting with structural failure leading to late IOL instability. Nearly half of confirmed cases presented without clinically evident spontaneous posterior capsular rupture, suggesting that rupture is not required for DBS diagnosis.

records.title: Monovision vs blended vision for presbyopia correction: prospective observational study.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Monovision vs blended vision for presbyopia correction: prospective observational study.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare visual outcomes, quality of life, and patient satisfaction between monovision with bilateral monofocal intraocular lenses (IOLs) and blended vision combining a trifocal IOL in the dominant eye with a monofocal IOL in the nondominant eye for presbyopia correction after cataract surgery.

Setting

Tertiary care ophthalmology center in Mumbai, India.

Design

Prospective observational study with masked outcome assessment.

Methods

A total of 150 patients with bilateral cataracts who desired postoperative spectacle independence were counselled regarding 2 surgical strategies: monovision with bilateral monofocal IOLs or blended vision (trifocal IOL in the dominant eye and monofocal IOL in the nondominant eye). After detailed counselling, patients selected their preferred strategy. Outcomes were assessed at 6 months postoperatively.

Results

At 6 months, the blended group demonstrated a significantly lower mean area under the curve compared with the monovision group (0.746 ± 0.130 vs 1.090 ± 0.295 logMAR·diopters, respectively, P < .001), indicating broader depth of focus. The National Eye Institute Visual Function Questionnaire-25 score was significantly higher in the blended vision group (89.1 ± 9.8 vs 83.6 ± 10.8; P = .001). Blended vision achieved better spectacle independence for distance, near, and intermediate tasks. Stereoacuity was significantly better preserved in blended vision. Blended vision, however, was linked to higher incidence of halos and decreased contrast sensitivity in both photopic and mesopic conditions.

Conclusions

Blended vision provides superior continuous range of vision, better quality of life, enhanced spectacle independence, and preserved stereoacuity compared with monovision, though at the cost of increased dysphotopsia and reduced contrast sensitivity.

records.title: Development of posterior vitreous detachment after lens surgery in myopic eyes - Results from the MYOPRED study.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Development of posterior vitreous detachment after lens surgery in myopic eyes - Results from the MYOPRED study.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the preoperative posterior vitreous detachment (PVD) status and PVD progression in myopic eyes without preexisting complete PVD after lens surgery.

Setting

10 European study centers.

Design

Prospective observational multicenter study.

Methods

Eyes with an axial length of ≥25.0 mm scheduled for phacoemulsification were included. Preoperatively and at each visit, the PVD status was assessed by optical coherence tomography, at certain sites using additional ultrasonography. All patients had a follow-up visit 2 months postoperatively, those without preoperative complete PVD additionally at 6 and 12 months or until presence of complete PVD.

Results

In the analysis, 968 eyes (600 study eyes, 368 eligible fellow eyes) of 600 patients were considered. Mean age was 64.8±9.9 years (range 23-92), 290 (48.3%) were female, 310 (51.7%) male. At baseline, PVD was complete in 512 (52.9%) eyes, incomplete in 256 (26.4%), no PVD in 85 (8.8%) and 'not decisive' in 115 (11.9%). Of the eyes with no or incomplete PVD preoperatively, 9.9-12.6% developed a complete PVD by 2 months, 25.5% by 6 and 40.2% by 12 months (n=327). The hazard ratio for progression to complete PVD was 1.37 (CI 1.10-1.69, P=.003) for each decade of age and 1.25 (CI 1.11-1.54, P<.001) for each mm of axial length. PVD progression occurred in 48.0% of eyes within 12 months after surgery.

Conclusions

Four out of 10 myopic eyes with no or incomplete PVD preoperatively progressed to complete PVD within 1 year after phacoemulsification. Progression to complete PVD was associated with patient age and axial length.

records.title: Comparison of decentration, tilt, and dynamic stability between retropupillary iris claw and scleral-fixated intraocular lenses with flanged haptics.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Comparison of decentration, tilt, and dynamic stability between retropupillary iris claw and scleral-fixated intraocular lenses with flanged haptics.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare decentration, tilt, and dynamic stability ("wobble") between retropupillary-fixated iris claw intraocular lenses (IOLs) and double-needle flanged scleral-fixated technique.

Setting

Vienna Institute for Research in Ocular Surgery, Hanusch Hospital, Vienna, Austria.

Design

Monocentric comparative observational study.

Methods

Secondary IOL alignment was evaluated using swept source anterior segment optical coherence tomography to quantify decentration and tilt. Dynamic lens behavior was assessed using a Purkinje meter during 9-degree saccadic eye movements. Additional outcomes included visual acuity, refraction, and complications.

Results

72 eyes of 72 patients were included, comprising 31 eyes with retropupillary iris claw IOLs and 41 eyes with scleral-fixated IOLs. Mean decentration was similar between groups, with no statistically significant difference (598 ± 303 μm vs 535 ± 261 μm; P = .57). Mean tilt was lower in the iris claw group than in the scleral-fixated group, with a statistically significant difference between groups (6.52 ± 3.20 degrees vs 8.93 ± 5.02 degrees; P = .03). Across all gaze directions, iris claw lenses demonstrated greater dynamic instability, with larger postsaccadic oscillation amplitudes, longer stationary times, and lower damping ratios (all P < .001). Visual acuity, refraction, and complication rates were comparable between groups. The IOL-iris distance was smaller in the iris claw group.

Conclusions

Decentration was comparable, whereas iris claw lenses showed less tilt but greater dynamic instability than scleral-fixated lenses.

records.title: Ray-Tracing Aberrometry and the Dysfunctional Lens Index for Objective Assessment of Posterior Capsular Opacification.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Ray-Tracing Aberrometry and the Dysfunctional Lens Index for Objective Assessment of Posterior Capsular Opacification.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the dysfunctional lens index (DLI), higher-order aberrations (HOA), and modulation transfer function (MTF) from ray-tracing aberrometry as objective markers of posterior capsular opacification (PCO) and treatment response.

Setting

Two tertiary ophthalmology centers, Istanbul, Turkey.

Design

Prospective interventional study with a clear-capsule pseudophakic control group.

Methods

Eyes with visually significant PCO after uncomplicated phacoemulsification with monofocal IOL implantation underwent ray-tracing aberrometry and 4 weeks after Nd:YAG capsulotomy; one eye per patient was analysed. CDVA, DLI, total and internal HOA root mean square (RMS), Zernike components, and MTF at 5-30 cycles/degree (cpd) were compared with clear-capsule control eyes with the same IOL.

Results

Thirty-one eyes of 31 patients (mean age 66.7 years; 21 female) and 28 control eyes were included. All parameters improved after capsulotomy (all P<.001): CDVA from 0.52 to 0.10 logMAR, DLI from 3.10 to 7.20, internal HOA RMS by 66.9%. Internal coma and trefoil decreased, whereas spherical aberration was unchanged (negative control). MTF improved at all six spatial frequencies. Pre-operatively, PCO eyes were degraded relative to controls (DLI 3.35 vs 7.67; P<.001); post-operatively they matched controls (7.23 vs 7.67; P=.44). DLI correlated with internal HOA (r=-0.947) and MTF (r=+0.842) but not CDVA (r=-0.051).

Conclusions

Ray-tracing aberrometry offers an objective view of PCO-induced optical degradation. Because the DLI tracks internal aberrations and MTF yet remains independent of high-contrast acuity, it captures impairment that CDVA alone overlooks, and returns to clear-capsule levels after capsulotomy. The DLI thus serves as a useful adjunctive marker for gauging PCO-related degradation and monitoring treatment response.

records.title: INTRASCLERAL FIXATION WITH DOUBLE-FLANGED PROLENE: A Stable Technique for Intraocular Lens Implantation.

content.title: INTRASCLERAL FIXATION WITH DOUBLE-FLANGED PROLENE: A Stable Technique for Intraocular Lens Implantation.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the efficacy and safety of a double-flanged prolene (DFP) intrascleral fixation technique for intraocular lens (IOL) implantation in eyes lacking capsular support.

Methods

This retrospective study included 59 eyes (59 patients) undergoing IOL fixation through DFP (n = 30) or Yamane flanged (YF); n = 29 techniques (November 2019-January 2024). Surgical duration, intraocular time, best-corrected visual acuity, endothelial cell density, IOL position, and complications were assessed.

Results

The DFP group had shorter total surgical (32.70 ± 3.21 vs. 42.80 ± 2.63 minutes, P < 0.001) and intraocular times (4.42 ± 0.77 vs. 10.95 ± 0.82 minutes, P < 0.001). The median best-corrected visual acuity improved from 20/50 (Snellen) to 20/36 (Snellen) at the last visit ( P < 0.001), with a lower endothelial cell density loss (77.67 ± 16.22 vs. 216.45 ± 60.33 cells/mm 2 , P < 0.001). YF had higher complication rates (iridemia, cystoid macular edema, haptic exposure; P = 0.039). IOL tilt/decentration increased comparably in both groups.

Conclusion

The DFP technique offers a safe, efficient alternative to YF for IOL fixation in eyes without capsular support, providing stable positioning, improved visual outcomes, and reduced endothelial cell loss.

records.title: Corneal versus refractive surgically induced astigmatism: vector analysis of their dissociation and implications for toric IOL planning.

content.title: Corneal versus refractive surgically induced astigmatism: vector analysis of their dissociation and implications for toric IOL planning.
content.abstract: To determine whether tomographically measured surgically induced astigmatism (SIA) is reflected in the manifest refraction, and whether the ocular residual astigmatism (ORA) precedes surgery and is stable per eye. Single-center, longitudinal, comparative vector analysis. Eyes underwent non-toric intraocular lens (IOL) or phakic implantable collamer lens (ICL) implantation. Total corneal refractive power (Pentacam) and manifest subjective refractive astigmatism at the corneal plane were expressed as Cartesian double-angle power vectors before and 3 months after surgery, yielding tomographic SIA (tSIA), refractive SIA (rSIA), their vector difference ΔSIA, and the pre- and postoperative ORA. Each SIA was decomposed into its flattening effect and torque at the incision meridian. Centroids were tested against the null by eye side. Of 290 eyes (256 IOL; 34 ICL), tSIA magnitude was small (IOL 0.47D; ICL 0.34-0.39D) with centroids near null. ΔSIA had a large mean magnitude (IOL 0.74-0.88D) but a near-origin centroid, significant only in IOL right eyes. Mean corneal flattening effect (+0.008D right, +0.140D left eyes) did not predict its refractive counterpart. ORA did not differ between cohorts (-0.11D, 95%-CI -0.25 to +0.02) and remained significant postoperatively, yet per eye only half the offset persisted in phakic and less in pseudophakic eyes. The per-eye tSIA was uncorrelated with the refractive SIA and carried no systematic direction, as power vectors or flattening effect, which stayed below a quarter of a toric cylinder step. ORA preceded surgery and remained systematically stable. Individually measured tSIA has only limited value for toric IOL planning.

records.title: Biomechanical stiffening effect in ultra-high-fluence extracorporeal crosslinked corneal allogenic intrastromal ring segments.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Biomechanical stiffening effect in ultra-high-fluence extracorporeal crosslinked corneal allogenic intrastromal ring segments.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare the biomechanical stiffening effects of a new ultra-high-fluence corneal crosslinking (CXL) protocol with conventional high-fluence CXL for extracorporeal corneal allogenic intrastromal ring segment optimization (ECO-CAIRS).

Setting

ELZA Institute, Zurich, Switzerland.

Design

Experimental, randomized, controlled, ex vivo laboratory study using porcine corneas. No masking was applied.

Methods

84 porcine corneas were divided into 4 groups: Group A (control), Group B (10 J/cm 2 ), Group C (30 J/cm 2 ), and Group D (60 J/cm 2 ). After epithelial debridement, Groups B, C, and D were treated with 0.1% hypo-osmolar riboflavin. UV-A irradiation was delivered at fluences of 10 J/cm 2 (18 mW/cm 2 , 9:15 min) for Group B, 30 J/cm 2 (30 mW/cm 2 , 16:40 min) for Group C, and 60 J/cm 2 (30 mW/cm 2 , 33:18 min) for Group D. Corneal biomechanical properties were assessed by stress‑strain extensiometry.

Results

Mean elastic modulus (5% strain) values were as follows: Group A (1.39 ± 0.49 N/mm), Group B (1.83 ± 0.48 N/mm), Group C (2.25 ± 0.83 N/mm), and Group D (2.31 ± 0.88 N/mm). Ultra-high-fluence groups (C and D) showed significantly greater stiffening than Group B ( P = .041 and P = .015), with no significant difference between Groups C and D ( P = 1.00). Group B exhibited significantly greater stiffening than Group A ( P = .023).

Conclusions

Ultra-high-fluence CXL enhances biomechanical stiffening compared with conventional high-fluence CXL, supporting its use in ECO-CAIRS. In this extracorporeal context, endothelial safety and haze are irrelevant, while increased stiffness facilitates intrastromal ring insertion and reduces corneal swelling.

records.title: Effect of Dry Eye and Ocular Surface Treatment on Agreement and Repeatability of Corneal Astigmatism Measurements Among Three Devices.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Effect of Dry Eye and Ocular Surface Treatment on Agreement and Repeatability of Corneal Astigmatism Measurements Among Three Devices.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the effect of dry eye disease (DED) and ocular surface treatment on the agreement and repeatability of corneal astigmatism measurements obtained using IOLMaster 700, Pentacam, and iTrace in patients with age-related cataract.

Setting

Eye, Ear, Nose, and Throat Hospital of Fudan University, Shanghai, China.

Design

Prospective, single-center study.

Methods

A total of 313 eyes of patients with age-related cataract were included. Eyes with DED received 0.3% sodium hyaluronate eye drops for 2 weeks and were re-examined after treatment. Corneal astigmatism measurements were obtained using IOLMaster 700, Pentacam, and iTrace before pupil dilation. The main parameters included keratometric corneal astigmatism, total corneal astigmatism, and their vector components. Interdevice agreement was assessed using Bland-Altman analysis, and test-retest repeatability was evaluated using within-subject standard deviation, test-retest repeatability, and intraclass correlation coefficients.

Results

Compared with the control group, eyes at DED baseline showed wider limits of agreement and poorer TRT for both scalar astigmatism parameters and vector components. After ocular surface treatment, LoA width decreased by 50.5%-62.5% for KCA and 19.9%-29.0% for TCA across the three device comparisons. KCA repeatability improved significantly after treatment for IOLMaster 700 and iTrace, whereas significant improvement in TCA repeatability was observed only for IOLMaster 700. Device- and parameter-specific differences persisted after treatment.

Conclusions

DED was associated with reduced agreement and repeatability of corneal astigmatism measurements obtained using IOLMaster 700, Pentacam, and iTrace. Short-term ocular surface treatment was associated with improved measurement stability.

records.title: Continuity of Care and Long-Term Outcome Surveillance After Posterior Chamber Phakic IOL Implantation.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Continuity of Care and Long-Term Outcome Surveillance After Posterior Chamber Phakic IOL Implantation.
content.abstract: Posterior chamber phakic intraocular lenses have a strong short-to-medium-term safety profile on the modern central-port platform, and a 2025 US Food and Drug Administration expansion of the indicated age range for a central-port phakic IOL to 21 to 60 years widens the eligible population. These lenses are to remain in the eye for decades, yet the field has defined what to monitor without building the infrastructure to deliver that monitoring reliably as patients age, change providers, and relocate. Existing guidance specifies endothelial and vault thresholds but does not address who monitors after the implanting surgeon, how baseline and longitudinal data transfer, or how late events are learned across practices. We propose three measures: upgrading the implant identification card into a longitudinal, portable surveillance record; a risk-stratified, age-informed surveillance framework developed through multisociety consensus; and a prospective implant registry with a defined minimum dataset. The device's clinical maturation now requires a parallel evolution in its care model.

records.title: Long-Term Visual, Refractive, and Patient-Reported Satisfaction of the Tel-Aviv Protocol (ePRK-CXL) for Progressive Keratoconus.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Long-Term Visual, Refractive, and Patient-Reported Satisfaction of the Tel-Aviv Protocol (ePRK-CXL) for Progressive Keratoconus.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the long-term visual, refractive, and patient-reported satisfaction of epithelial photorefractive keratectomy (ePRK) combined with corneal cross-linking (CXL) - the Tel-Aviv Protocol - in patients with progressive keratoconus.

Setting

Care-Vision Laser Center, Tel Aviv, Israel.

Design

Retrospective, single-center case series.

Methods

Consecutive patients with progressive keratoconus who underwent ePRK-CXL were included. Preoperative and last-available postoperative pachymetry, keratometry (Kmean, Kmin, Kmax), spherical equivalent (SEQ), manifest refraction, uncorrected distance visual acuity (UDVA), and corrected distance visual acuity (CDVA) were recorded; safety and efficacy indices were calculated. Patient-reported outcomes regarding spectacle/contact lens dependence, satisfaction, and visual symptoms were assessed with a structured questionnaire.

Results

Fifty eyes of 38 patients (mean age 25.9±6.8 years) were followed for a mean of 2,910±605 days (∼8 years; range 5-12). UDVA improved from 1.04±0.70 to 0.36±0.37 logMAR and CDVA from 0.23±0.16 to 0.11±0.10 logMAR (both P < 0.001); safety and efficacy indices were 1.42±0.55 and 0.93±0.51. K-max decreased from 47.51±2.96 to 45.95±2.99 D and SEQ from -2.42±2.29 to -0.82±1.57 D (both P < 0.001). Pachymetry decreased from 448.65±38.95 to 418.93±55.77 μm. Overall satisfaction was high (81.6% satisfied/very satisfied), 76.3% reported subjective visual improvement, 52.6% achieved spectacle independence, and 92.1% required no contact lenses. No progression was observed in the examined eyes.

Conclusions

At a mean follow-up of ∼8 years, the Tel-Aviv Protocol provided durable visual and refractive improvement, stabilized keratometry without progression, and yielded high patient satisfaction with low symptom burden. These results support ePRK-CXL as a tissue-sparing option for progressive keratoconus.

records.title: Resident to Urgent Eye Clinic Transformation and Association With Health Equity and Resident Education.

content.title: Resident to Urgent Eye Clinic Transformation and Association With Health Equity and Resident Education.
content.abstract:
Importance

US ophthalmology residency programs are divided between traditional resident clinic-based models with a separate faculty practice, and universal practice-based models. Little data exist comparing these educational models.

Objective

To evaluate the association of changing a traditional resident clinic training model to a universal practice plus urgent eye clinic-based residency training model with sociodemographic disparities and resident education.

Design, setting, and participants

This was a cross-sectional study conducted at a US academic medical center. All patients presenting to the University of Rochester Flaum Eye Institute between the period July 1, 2017, to June 30, 2019, and the period July 1, 2022, to June 30, 2024, were divided into 4 cohorts for retrospective analysis as follows: resident clinic 2017-2019, faculty practice 2017-2019, urgent eye clinic 2022-2024, and universal practice 2022-2024.

Exposures

The resident clinic was transitioned to urgent eye clinic in July 2022. All former patients from resident clinic were reassigned to the new universal practice.

Main outcomes and measures

Patient cohorts were compared regarding insurance payor(s) and self-identified race. Level of disease acuity in resident clinic and urgent eye clinic were compared. Graduating resident procedural volumes were compared.

Results

Participants were divided into the following 4 cohorts: resident clinic 2017-2019 (6819 patients), faculty practice 2017-2019 (61 847 patients), urgent eye clinic 2022-2024 (5124 patients), and universal practice 2022-2024 (79 001 patients), for a total of 118 459 patients (mean [SD] age, 47 [25] years; 65 186 female [55%]). Pretransition, compared with faculty practice patients, greater proportions of resident clinic patients used Medicaid insurance (62.1% vs 19.4%; difference, 32.0%; 95% CI, 30.9%-33.1%; P < .001) and identified as Asian, Black or African American, multiracial, native (ie, American Indian or Alaska Native), or other (51.9% vs 23.6%; difference, 28.3%; 95% CI, 27.1%-29.5%; P < .001). Posttransition, compared with universal practice patients, similar proportions of urgent eye clinic patients used Medicaid insurance (26.8% vs 27.8%; difference, 0.4%; 95% CI, -0.7% to 1.6%; P = .42) and identified as Asian, Black or African American, multiracial, native, or other (29.6% vs 26.8%; difference, 2.8%; 95% CI, 1.5%-4.1%; P < .001). A greater proportion of urgent eye clinic patients presented with high-acuity disease (37.6%) compared with resident clinic patients (20.9%; difference, 16.7%; 95% CI, 15.0%-18.4%; P < .001). Median graduating resident primary cataract surgery volume increased from 148 to 228 cases (difference, 80; 95% CI, 49 to 122; P < .001).

Conclusions and relevance

Results of this cross-sectionals study show that transforming resident clinic into urgent eye clinic was associated with reduced sociodemographic disparities, enhanced resident exposure to high-acuity disease, and increased resident procedural experience. These results suggest that changes in resident clinic structure may improve both health equity and resident education.

records.title: Diabetes Severity in Cornea Donors and 1-Year Outcomes in Recipients in the Diabetes Endothelial Keratoplasty Study: A Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Clinical Trial.

content.title: Diabetes Severity in Cornea Donors and 1-Year Outcomes in Recipients in the Diabetes Endothelial Keratoplasty Study: A Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Clinical Trial.
content.abstract:
Importance

The effect of cornea donor diabetes severity on graft success, endothelial cell density (ECD), and morphometry after Descemet membrane endothelial keratoplasty (DMEK) is not known.

Objective

To determine whether graft success, corneal endothelial cell loss (ECL), and morphometric changes 1 year after DMEK are associated with cornea donor diabetes severity measured by severity score, donor's postmortem level of hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), and postmortem advanced glycation end products (AGEs) or advanced oxidation end products (AOPs).

Design, setting, and participants

This was a secondary analysis of a multicenter, double-masked, randomized clinical trial at 28 clinical sites (46 surgeons) and 13 eye banks in the US among individuals undergoing low- to moderate-risk DMEK. AGE and AOP measurements were collected from a subset of donors. Data analysis was conducted from September 1, 2025, through April 30, 2026.

Intervention

DMEK performed with a cornea from a donor without or with diabetes, assigned using a minimization procedure (comparable to randomization) to achieve an approximate 2:1 distribution, respectively.

Main outcomes and measures

Graft success, ECL, coefficient of variation (CV) of cell area, and percentage of hexagonal cells (HEX) at 1 year from eye bank and postoperative specular central endothelial images.

Results

A total of 1097 individuals (1421 study eyes; median [IQR] age, 71 [66-76] years; 631 [57.5%] female) undergoing low- to moderate-risk DMEK (1044 [95.2%] for Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy) were included. AGE and AOP measurements were collected from a subset of 472 donors (542 study donor corneas). Among 968 eyes with a postmortem donor HbA1c level lower than 6.5%, the 1-year graft success rate was 97.1% (95% CI, 95.4%-98.4%), compared with 97.4% (95% CI, 93.9%-100.0%), 93.0% (95% CI, 83.3%-98.8%), and 95.8% (95% CI, 87.3%-100.0%) among eyes with a donor HbA1c level of 6.5% to less than 7.5% (n = 194), 7.5% to less than 9.0% (n = 86), and 9.0% or higher (n = 48), respectively (P = .72). There was no significant difference in mean ECD across donor HbA1c groups. Donor diabetes severity measured with severity score, donor HbA1c level, and AGE and AOP metrics was not associated with 1-year graft failure, ECD, CV in cell area, or HEX percentage.

Conclusions and relevance

This secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial found that ECL and morphometry 1 year after DMEK were not affected by cornea donor diabetes severity. Comparable 1-year graft success, ECL, and cell morphometrics with tissue from donors with and without diabetes, regardless of the diabetes severity biomarker values observed, support the use of corneas from donors with diabetes for endothelial keratoplasty procedures without additional preoperative testing or risk stratification based on the diabetes status of the cornea donor.

Trial registration

ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05134480.

records.title: Validation of the University of California, Irvine Corneal Cystine Crystal Score (UCI CCCS): Correlations with Clinical, Imaging, and Symptom Outcomes in Cystinosis.

content.title: Validation of the University of California, Irvine Corneal Cystine Crystal Score (UCI CCCS): Correlations with Clinical, Imaging, and Symptom Outcomes in Cystinosis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To prospectively validate the University of California, Irvine Corneal Cystine Crystal Score (UCI CCCS), a standardized slit-lamp grading tool, by evaluating associations with objective corneal densitometry, patient-reported symptoms, and visual acuity in a real-world cystinosis cohort.

Design

Prospective observational cross-sectional study.

Participants

Seventy patients (140 eyes) with confirmed cystinosis were examined at the 2024-2025 Cystinosis Research Foundation Day of Hope Clinics.

Methods

All eyes underwent live slit-lamp UCI CCCS grading (0-5). Pentacam Scheimpflug densitometry was obtained in 68 eyes. Two ophthalmologists independently graded patients during the 2025 clinic to assess inter-rater reliability. Patient-reported symptoms, best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), and topical cysteamine treatment data were collected. Linear mixed-effects models accounting for within-patient correlation were used for densitometry and BCVA analyses. Symptom associations were evaluated at the patient level using Kendall's tau-b.

Main outcome measures

Inter-rater reliability of UCI CCCS; associations with corneal densitometry, patient-reported symptoms, and BCVA.

Results

Inter-rater reliability was excellent (ICC = 0.995; 95% CI, 0.992-0.996). Linear mixed-effects modeling demonstrated significant associations between UCI CCCS grade and central (p = 0.0016) and anterior corneal densitometry (p = 0.0011) after accounting for within-patient correlation between fellow eyes. Higher UCI CCCS grades were significantly associated with greater photophobia (τ = 0.397, p < 0.0001), foreign-body sensation (τ = 0.295, p = 0.0047), and ocular dryness (τ = 0.405, p = 0.0001). No statistically significant association was observed between UCI CCCS grade and BCVA after accounting for within-patient correlation (p = 0.4389). No significant differences in UCI CCCS or corneal densitometry were observed across topical cysteamine treatment groups.

Conclusion

The UCI CCCS is a highly reproducible, clinically practical grading tool associated with objective corneal densitometry and patient-reported symptom burden, while BCVA was not significantly associated with UCI CCCS grade. Longitudinal studies are needed to evaluate treatment responsiveness and prognostic value.

records.title: Comparison of refractive surgeries (SMILE, LASIK, and PRK) with and without corneal crosslinking: systematic review and meta-analysis.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Comparison of refractive surgeries (SMILE, LASIK, and PRK) with and without corneal crosslinking: systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract: Corneal crosslinking (CXL) is used for treating keratoconus and post-laser in situ keratomileusis ectasia. However, refractive surgery is not usually performed with prophylactic CXL. Therefore, we performed a meta-analysis comparing outcomes of refractive surgeries with vs without prophylactic CXL. We systematically searched databases for studies comparing refractive surgeries for myopic correction with vs without prophylactic corneal crosslinking. Review Manager 5.4.1 was used to perform statistical analysis. We included 2820 eyes from 28 studies. Compared with refractive surgery alone, surgery with prophylactic CXL resulted in decreased central corneal thickness, corrected distance visual acuity logMAR, and safety and efficacy indices. There were no significant differences in postoperative uncorrected distance visual acuity of 20/20 or better at ≥12 months and other visual outcomes among both groups. More randomized controlled trials with standard crosslinking protocols are needed to analyze the prophylactic use of crosslinking with refractive surgeries.

records.title: Efficacy, safety, and predictability of transepithelial vs mechanical or alcohol-assisted photorefractive keratectomy: meta-analysis.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Efficacy, safety, and predictability of transepithelial vs mechanical or alcohol-assisted photorefractive keratectomy: meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Topic

The aim of this study was to assess the meta-analysis of the studies comparing transepithelial photorefractive keratectomy (transPRK) with classic photorefractive keratectomy (PRK) (mechanical or alcohol-assisted).

Clinical relevance

Although PRK is a well-established procedure, transPRK, a newer, minimally invasive technique may reduce surgery time and improve patient outcomes. Comparing these techniques helps optimize surgical choices.

Methods

Relevant studies were collected from PubMed and were included if they met the following criteria: comparison of transPRK and PRK in efficacy, safety, predictability, correction index, difference vector, or index of success. The odds ratio (OR) estimates, risk ratio, and 95% CIs were derived from random-effects meta-analysis.

Results

20 studies with a total of 10 204 treated eyes were included in this meta-analysis. The pooled estimates between transPRK and PRK were as follows: log(OR) of the efficacy had a value of 0 (CI -0.32 to 0.33), log(OR) of the safety was 0.04 (CI -0.98 to 1.06), and log(OR) of the predictability was 0.48 (CI 0.16-0.81).

Conclusions

This meta-analysis showed that there were no statistically significant differences in either of the visual outcomes (efficacy, efficacy index, safety, safety index, and predictability). Although transPRK is preferred for its minimally invasive approach and quicker recovery, PRK continues to be a reliable option, particularly in environments where advanced technology is not easily affordable. The choice of laser platform can also influence the surgical outcomes through features such as advanced pulse technology, optimized ablation speed, and profiles.

records.title: Safety and Efficacy of Posterior Chamber Phakic Implantable Collamer Lenses in Patients with Keratoconus: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Safety and Efficacy of Posterior Chamber Phakic Implantable Collamer Lenses in Patients with Keratoconus: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To assess the safety and efficacy of phakic implantable collamer lenses (ICLs) in patients with keratoconus.

Design

Systematic review and meta-analysis.

Methods

We conducted a pre- and postintervention single-arm systematic review and meta-analysis in line with guidelines from the Cochrane Collaboration and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 Consensus Statement. We searched five electronic databases and the grey literature for any studies evaluating ICLs in the setting of keratoconus. Our primary outcomes were the corrected distance visual acuity, uncorrected distance visual acuity, and manifest cylinder astigmatism.
